subject: Most appropriate distance metric for mixed-ploidy (diploid and polyploid) SNP data?

messages.author: d7b556bd4c296501
messages.subject: Most appropriate distance metric for mixed-ploidy (diploid and polyploid) SNP data?
parts:
Hello Poppr's!

I've been using Poppr successfully (I hope) to look at population structure in my mixed-ploidy SNP data by importing each ploidy level (diploid, triploid, and tetraploid) into a separate genind object and then pooling into a combined genind. This has allowed me to detect clonality and MLGs (my polyploids are also asexual), as well as use PCA/DAPC and K-means clustering. I know that multivariate approaches can allow me to bypass some of the assumption-breaking aspects of my data, but I would now like to construct some trees, calculate population differentiation statistics, and look at pair-wise distances between individuals. From what I can tell, all of these require some sort of distance matrix, of which I know Poppr offers several options. However, according to "The Analysis of Polyploid Genetic Data" (Meirmans et al 2018), all of the distance metrics they evaluated are biased for mixed ploidy analyses, and should be avoided (but apparently the relatedness coefficients are unbiased?). On the other hand, Meirmans and Liu (2018) suggest using squared Euclidian distances to calculate AMOVA and rho, which is supposed to be OK for mixed-ploidy datasets. I understand that the theory from this paper been incorporated into Poppr in the poppr.amova() function, which is great. All of that said, I have a few questions:

1) Is there a suitable distance metric I can use in Poppr to look at pairwise differences between individuals in my mixed-ploidy dataset? I'd mainly like to use this to create a distance tree to assess the number of origins of asexuality in my species (by looking at asexual lineages nested with sexual populations on the tree). I cannot use Bruvo distance as I do not have microsatellite data, and Meirmans et al 2018 reported that Bruvo distance is biased anyways...If not, is there a way to calculate "relatedness coefficients" in Poppr as discussed in Meirmans et al 2018?

2) Is it possible to do a pairwise AMOVA between all of the populations in my dataset in Poppr? I saw that there was an open issue somewhere on github for this, but I'm not sure if it's been implemented (or whether there's a workaround to do it manually...). 

3) This is only semi-related to the above topic, but a few of the analyses I've attempted to do requires me to convert my genind to genpop. However, I receive an error from genind2genpop that "conversion to genpop not supported for varying ploidy". Is there any workaround for this?

Thanks in advance for any advice you may have!

Evan

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Most appropriate distance metric for mixed-ploidy (diploid and polyploid) SNP data?
parts:
Hi Evan,

I'll see if I can do my best to answer these questions:

1) Is there a suitable distance metric I can use in Poppr to look at pairwise differences between individuals in my mixed-ploidy dataset? I'd mainly like to use this to create a distance tree to assess the number of origins of asexuality in my species (by looking at asexual lineages nested with sexual populations on the tree). I cannot use Bruvo distance as I do not have microsatellite data, and Meirmans et al 2018 reported that Bruvo distance is biased anyways...If not, is there a way to calculate "relatedness coefficients" in Poppr as discussed in Meirmans et al 2018?

I'm afraid that there is no current method to calculate relatedness in poppr. It looks like POLYRELATEDNESS is available on Github, but not as the source code, but rather as a zipped up binary, so YMMV unfortunately https://github.com/huangkang1987/polyrelatedness. If someone were to dive into the weeds of Huang 2014 and create a function that can return a reasonable similarity distance, I would be more than happy to help them to get that into poppr.

2) Is it possible to do a pairwise AMOVA between all of the populations in my dataset in Poppr? I saw that there was an open issue somewhere on github for this, but I'm not sure if it's been implemented (or whether there's a workaround to do it manually...).

That's unfortunately another thing I haven't really had the bandwidth to work on. You should be able to get a list of AMOVA objects with something like this (replacing the relevant bits with your own data and strata):

pop_combinations <- combn(popNames(myData), 2)
amova_list <- apply(pop_combinations, MARGIN = 2, function(i) poppr.amova(myData[pop = i], ~Pop))

3) This is only semi-related to the above topic, but a few of the analyses I've attempted to do requires me to convert my genind to genpop. However, I receive an error from genind2genpop that "conversion to genpop not supported for varying ploidy". Is there any workaround for this?

The heart of the conversion is in this line of code: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/blob/0c9dc83f041561edb516fcada9c050ca1da00c57/R/genind2genpop.R#L106-L107

From there, you will get a matrix that you can pass to new("genpop", myMatrix, ploidy = N, type = "codom"). I believe the restriction was put there simply because working with mixed-ploidies violates a whole slew of assumptions, so YMMV.

Best,
Zhian

Thanks for getting back to be so quickly, Zhian! I'll try out your suggestions and report back if I run into any issues. My first goal is attempting to export my data from Poppr to PolyRelatedness and back again.

For data import into PolyRelatedness, I need to feed it a text file where missing data are recorded as 0's, and the alleles are listed as positive integers. I'm able to get the data into the correct format using genind2df, but my data are encoded as 0's (reference allele) and 1's (alternate allele) -- these were originally converted from vcf files using vcfR2genind. Do you know of a way I can easily convert to the format I need for PolyRelatedness?

e.g. for a triploid

000 -> 111

or

011 -> 122

e.g. convert NA's:

NA -> 00 (for diploid)
NA -> 000 (for triploid)

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: Most appropriate distance metric for mixed-ploidy (diploid and polyploid) SNP data?
parts:
Hi Evan,

Sorry I'm only getting to this now. I have been in HAM mode for the past week preparing for UseR! 2019.

1. You will be better off just using `vcfR::extract.gt()` and manipulating that instead of first converting to a genind object
2. You get back a character matrix with samples in COLUMNS and loci in ROWS, so you will need to transpose that matrix with `t()`
3. use the following to convert your data
   my_gt[] <- gsub("[/|]", "", my_gt) # remove separators
   my_gt[] <- gsub("1", "2", my_gt) # change 1 to 2
   my_gt[] <- gsub("0", "1", my_gt) # change 0 to 1
   my_gt[] <- gsub("\\.", "0", my_gt) # change . to 0
4. Export to your heart's desire.

Best,
Zhian
